subject: Task 21.1 — version bump and release metadata (build.yaml / Directory.Build.props -> 1.2.0.0) and the four plugin-version test literals in PluginPackagingTests.cs, PluginDiscoveryHostTests.cs, PluginStateLocationTests.cs
audited_commit_state: Working tree at 679b694 with the 7 modified tracked files of task 21.1 uncommitted (build.yaml, Directory.Build.props, PLANS.md, docs/plan/state.json, and the three test files). No test or implementation file was modified by this audit.

findings.detail: Only the build.yaml half of the acceptance criterion ('the version is 1.2.0.0 in build.yaml and Directory.Build.props') is covered by an automated guard; the Directory.Build.props half is verified by no test, no MSBuild target, and no docs check.
findings.description: The acceptance criterion names two version sources. The suite guards exactly one of them: PluginPackagingTests.BuildManifestKeepsPinnedIdentityAndAbi asserts the literal 'version: "1.2.0.0"' in build.yaml. A repository-wide search of tests/ finds no reference to Directory.Build.props, <Version>, AssemblyVersion, or FileVersion for the plugin (the only FileVersion assertion in the suite is SkiaHostCompatibilityTests.cs:72 for SkiaSharp 3.119.4.0), and src/ArrTags/ArrTags.csproj has no target that cross-checks the props against build.yaml. Directory.Build.props sets <Version>, <AssemblyVersion> and <FileVersion> as three independent literals, so nothing but human/agent diff review keeps them equal to build.yaml. Consequence: a half-completed or later botched bump (e.g. props left at 1.1.0.0, or a typo in AssemblyVersion only) would leave the entire default suite green — the build would still succeed, all 1927 tests would pass — while shipping a package whose ArrTags.dll reports a different version than the build.yaml manifest Jellyfin reads. The shipped artifact's version is therefore an inspection-only fact, not a test-established one. Current state is in fact consistent (independently verified below), so this is a forward-looking false-confidence risk rather than a present defect.
evidence: git diff -- tests/ shows the only assertion-level change is PluginPackagingTests.cs:28 (build.yaml literal).

grep for 'Directory.Build.props|<Version>|AssemblyVersion|FileVersion' over tests/ returns exactly one hit, tests/ArrTags.Tests/SkiaHostCompatibilityTests.cs:72, which asserts SkiaSharp's FileVersion, not ArrTags'.

Directory.Build.props:4-6 sets <Version>, <AssemblyVersion> and <FileVersion> as three separate literals; src/ArrTags/ArrTags.csproj:100 only copies build.yaml into the staging directory and never compares it to $(Version).
scripts/check-docs.sh contains no version-consistency section (grep for 'version|build.yaml' returns nothing).

Independent verification of the current state (read-only): `unzip -o -q artifacts/ArrTags_1.2.0.0.zip ArrTags.dll build.yaml -d /tmp/final-review/test-quality/pkg` then `strings .../ArrTags.dll | grep -x '1.2.0.0'` -> 1.2.0.0, and the packaged build.yaml line 4 is `version: "1.2.0.0"`. The two sources do agree today.
findings.recommended_action: Add one unguarded fact (no host or archive dependency) beside BuildManifestKeepsPinnedIdentityAndAbi that reads Directory.Build.props and asserts that <Version>, <AssemblyVersion> and <FileVersion> all equal the version literal parsed out of build.yaml — a relative assertion, so it does not need updating on the next bump and does not duplicate a hard-coded constant. Optionally assert the same equality against typeof(Plugin).Assembly.GetName().Version so the compiled identity is checked too. Not a release blocker for v1.2: the three props are literally 1.2.0.0 and the compiled assembly reports 1.2.0.0.

findings.detail: The three [PackagedPluginFact] facts select the archive by ordinal-last filename and never assert the packaged build.yaml's version, so they can pass against a stale package.
findings.description: PluginPackagingPaths.TryFindPackageArchive enumerates artifacts/ArrTags_*.zip, orders by StringComparer.Ordinal and takes .Last(). With 1.0.1.0, 1.1.0.0 and 1.2.0.0 present this happens to select 1.2.0.0, but ordinal ordering is not numeric ordering (a future ArrTags_1.10.0.0.zip would sort before ArrTags_1.9.0.0.zip), and artifacts/ is gitignored so stale archives accumulate. None of the three packaged facts inspects the manifest inside the archive: PackageContainsTheRequiredPluginRootFiles only asserts the build.yaml entry exists and is non-empty, PackageHoldsEveryArtifactNamedInTheBuildManifest compares the archive against the repository build.yaml, and PackageDoesNotContainTheDuplicateSkiaSharpRuntime is a negative check. An archive built at 1.1.0.0 therefore satisfies all seven PluginPackagingTests facts today, including after a version bump. The worker's 'packaged build.yaml carries version 1.2.0.0' evidence came from a manual `unzip -p | grep`, not from the suite. This is pre-existing structure, not introduced by 21.1, and the worker disclosed the ordinal-last selection; it is recorded because the release-identity claim leans on these facts.
evidence: tests/ArrTags.Tests/PluginPackagingTests.cs:78-120 — the three packaged facts assert entry presence, artifact coverage, and SkiaSharp absence; none reads the archive's build.yaml version.
artifacts/ holds ArrTags_1.0.1.0.zip, ArrTags_1.1.0.0.zip and ArrTags_1.2.0.0.zip (gitignored), so the selector is choosing among accumulated archives.
docs/implementation/21.1/worker-report.json:16 records the packaged-version check as a manual `unzip -p artifacts/ArrTags_1.2.0.0.zip build.yaml | grep`.
findings.recommended_action: Either make the packaged facts read the archive's build.yaml and assert its version matches the repository manifest, or select the archive by parsing build.yaml's version (ArrTags_<version>.zip) instead of ordinal-last. Track as a Phase 21/22 test-strengthening item; it does not affect the correctness of the 1.2.0.0 bump.

summary: The 21.1 test edits are honest and do not weaken the suite. The one assertion-level change, PluginPackagingTests.cs:28, is a real and non-vacuous guard: the worker proved it non-vacuous by reverting build.yaml to 1.1.0.0 and observing the failure, and the assertion reads build.yaml from disk at run time, so a future un-mirrored version change fails the default suite. The other three literal changes are inert fixture mirrors whose value no assertion depends on; the worker disclosed exactly this, and I confirmed it by reading DerivePluginName and SeedVersionedInstall. Determinism and isolation are unaffected: all three files read repository files or use Guid-named temp roots with ordinal comparisons, and no new or widened skip was introduced (66 unchanged). Guard honesty holds — the 2 host-gated facts whose literal changed were skipped in every recorded run and are not counted as verification, the 3 packaged-archive facts really did run against the produced 1.2.0.0 archive, and both gate attributes fail rather than skip when misconfigured. Two gaps are recorded and neither blocks the release: TQ-21.1-01 (MEDIUM) — the Directory.Build.props half of the acceptance criterion has no automated guard at all, and its three version properties are independent literals, so a partial bump would pass the whole suite while shipping a mismatched assembly version (I verified independently that the current build.yaml and the compiled ArrTags.dll both report 1.2.0.0, so the present state is correct); and TQ-21.1-02 (LOW) — the packaged-archive facts select the archive by ordinal-last filename and never assert the packaged manifest's version, so they would also pass against a stale 1.1.0.0 archive. The remaining three items are informational: inert fixture literals in host-gated facts, configuration-dependent skip counts with the release matrix still owned by 21.3, and metadata prose that no test asserts (spot-checked as non-overclaiming). No BLOCKER or HIGH finding is open and the changed tests remain honest, meaningful within their scope, and deterministic, so the status is PASS_WITH_FINDINGS.
